required_components: strongest-interface lower bound with equal total information
strongest-parent product refusal or exact contraction

theorems.name: canonical-profile injectivity
theorems.statement_digest_text: For antichain warrant profiles, equal full revocation signatures imply equal canonical profiles.

theorems.name: zero-query summary lower bound
theorems.statement_digest_text: An exact zero-query summary needs at least the log2 number of admitted revocation-equivalence classes.

theorems.name: exponential counterfactual-warrant gap
theorems.statement_digest_text: Profiles sharing one valid current middle-layer warrant realize 2^(C(n,floor(n/2))-1) future signatures and shatter C(n,floor(n/2))-1 revocations.

theorems.name: exact storage-query frontier
theorems.statement_digest_text: In the coordinate-query model for the fixed-certificate family, exact completion requires and achieves S+Q=C(n,floor(n/2))-1.

theorems.name: direct sum across reusable skills
theorems.statement_digest_text: m independently warranted skills have joint revocation-shattering dimension and exact storage-query lower bound m(C(n,floor(n/2))-1).

theorems.name: positive-witness omission theorem
theorems.statement_digest_text: Every proper positive-only subfamily of an antichain admits a revocation killing all emitted warrants while preserving an omitted warrant.

theorems.name: bounded positive-witness insufficiency
theorems.statement_digest_text: For every k, k displayed positive witnesses can hide a (k+1)st warrant that changes a future revocation decision.

theorems.name: single-proof over-retraction
theorems.statement_digest_text: Revoking the displayed proof can leave an unobserved alternate warrant live.

theorems.name: one fixed-size warrant information bound
theorems.statement_digest_text: One unknown d-subset warrant among n atoms needs exactly ceil(log2 C(n,d)) bits for zero-query arbitrary revocation.

theorems.name: full-antichain sufficiency
theorems.statement_digest_text: The complete canonical warrant antichain exactly decides liveness after every admitted revocation.

theorems.name: false-retain false-retract abstain trilemma
theorems.statement_digest_text: A non-complete deterministic summary forces false retention, false retraction, or abstention on a decidable compatible instance.

theorems.name: semantic-learning revision separation
theorems.statement_digest_text: Fixed operator semantics and one identical current proof can coexist with exponentially many post-revocation library states.
